clues: Basophilic clumps visible in the cytoplasm of neuronal cell bodies and dendrites under light microscopy.
They are absent from the axon hillock and the axon itself.
Ultrastructurally, they represent stacks of rough endoplasmic reticulum and polyribosomes.
A sensory neuron whose single short stem bifurcates into a peripheral process and a central process.
It develops from a bipolar neuroblast whose two processes fuse during embryogenesis.
Its spherical cell bodies reside in dorsal root ganglia and sensory cranial nerve ganglia.
The largest and most numerous star-shaped neuroglial cell in the central nervous system.
Its radiating processes form perivascular end-feet around capillaries and express GFAP.
It regulates extracellular potassium and neurotransmitters and forms glial scars after CNS injury.
A neuroectoderm-derived glial cell predominant in the white matter of the brain and spinal cord.
It appears under H&E staining as a small dark round nucleus surrounded by a clear perinuclear halo.
One cell extends processes to myelinate segments of up to 50 different CNS axons simultaneously.
Small elongated glial cells with dark rod-shaped nuclei and thorny processes in the CNS.
Unlike other neuroglia, they originate from mesodermal yolk sac myeloid progenitors.
They serve as the resident phagocytes and antigen-presenting immune cells of the brain and spinal cord.
Cuboidal-to-columnar neuroepithelial cells arranged as a single layer without a typical basement membrane.
Their apical surfaces bear cilia and microvilli that help circulate cerebrospinal fluid.
They line the ventricles of the brain and the central canal of the spinal cord.

terms.sub: Peripheral Nervous System Glia and Myelin
clues: A periodic unmyelinated gap situated between adjacent Schwann cell or oligodendrocyte internodes.
The axolemma at this site has an exceptionally high density of voltage-gated sodium channels.
It enables rapid saltatory conduction of action potentials along myelinated nerve fibers.
The middle connective tissue sleeve surrounding an individual fascicle of peripheral nerve fibers.
It consists of concentric layers of flattened epithelioid myofibroblasts joined by tight junctions.
It acts as the metabolically active blood-nerve barrier protecting the endoneurial space.
A reversible reactive change occurring in a neuronal cell body following transection or severe crush of its axon.
The perikaryon swells with water and the nucleus is pushed to the cell periphery.
Basophilic Nissl bodies disperse as polyribosomes switch to synthesizing structural proteins for axon regrowth.
A large, ovoid encapsulated mechanoreceptor found in the deep dermis, hypodermis, and mesenteries.
In histological cross-section, its concentric cellular lamellae resemble a sliced onion.
It is a rapidly adapting receptor sensitive to high-frequency vibration and deep pressure.
